name: Sumac-Blackened Salmon with Citrus Salsa
why: Sumac is having a moment — this tangy Middle Eastern spice replaces traditional blackening seasoning for a bright, citrusy crust on salmon. Ready in 25 minutes, it's elegant enough for a dinner party but easy enough for a Tuesday.
author: Henry
ingredients: 2 to 2 1/2 lb side of salmon (skin-on or skinless)
2 large navel oranges, peeled and finely diced
1/2 small red onion, very thinly sliced
Zest and juice of 1 small lemon (about 2 tbsp juice)
Salt and black pepper, to taste

steps: Heat oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
Lay the salmon flat on the baking sheet (skin-side down if using skin-on) and brush evenly with olive oil.
In a small bowl, whisk together sumac, garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt, cumin, oregano, and black pepper until evenly combined.
Sprinkle the spice mixture evenly over the salmon, gently patting it down with your hands so it adheres.
Bake the salmon for 12–15 minutes, until it reaches an internal temperature of 125°F (52°C) in the thickest part and flakes easily with a fork.
Transfer the baking sheet to a wire rack and let the salmon rest for 5 minutes.
While the salmon bakes, gently toss the diced oranges, cucumber, red onion, cilantro, lemon zest, and lemon juice together in a small bowl.
Taste and season with salt and pepper (or extra lemon juice, if needed) to your liking.
Flake the salmon into generous portions and serve over cooked rice with avocado slices.
Top with the citrus salsa and an extra pinch of sumac for brightness.

pro_tips: Sumac has a bright, lemony-tart flavor — if you can't find it at your local store, it's widely available online. A good substitute is extra lemon zest plus a splash of pomegranate molasses.
Don't overcook the salmon — pull it at 125°F internal temp. It will continue cooking while resting and finish at the perfect 130–135°F.
